skill.description: Helps agents diagnose network failures and retry approved developer commands through a local proxychains4 proxy.
skill.summary: Route approved network commands through a local proxychains4 configuration when direct access fails.

security_audit.summary: The skill is a transparent proxychains helper, not malware, and most static hits are documentation examples or expected user-level proxy configuration. The confirmed risk is that it encourages broad and sometimes automatic proxy routing, including blocked HTTP responses, SOCKS proxy chains, privileged setup commands, and persistent wrappers.

remediation.issue: Automatic proxy wrapping can bypass access-control decisions.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before retrying a failed or blocked request through proxychains, especially after HTTP 403 or 451 responses.

remediation.issue: Privileged package-manager and system configuration commands appear in setup examples.
remediation.suggestion: Separate privileged setup from automatic skill behavior and require confirmation before any sudo command is executed or suggested as the next step.

remediation.issue: Persistent proxied shells and wrapper scripts can affect future commands.
remediation.suggestion: Label wrapper and startup examples as advanced optional steps, include rollback instructions, and avoid silent shell startup changes.

remediation.issue: Connectivity tests use public services such as Google and IP information endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Make external tests optional and provide a way to use organization-approved internal endpoints instead.

content.value_statement: Network failures can block package installs, repository access, and diagnostics. This skill helps agents retry approved commands through a local proxychains4 proxy.
actual_capabilities: Identifies common network failures such as timeouts, DNS errors, and connection refusals.
Suggests proxychains4 retries for Git, curl, wget, pip, npm, Docker, and SSH commands.
Provides a local proxychains configuration using 127.0.0.1:9910 as the default proxy.
Includes troubleshooting steps for proxy service checks, DNS behavior, and configuration errors.
Provides optional setup guidance for HTTP, SOCKS4, SOCKS5, strict, dynamic, and random proxy chains.
limitations: It does not start or provide a proxy service; users must operate the proxy endpoint themselves.
Proxychains supports TCP traffic only and may not work with static binaries or special network libraries.
Proxying commands can conflict with organization policy or service access rules.
Connectivity tests contact public endpoints unless the user replaces them with approved internal targets.

use_cases.description: Retry approved package and repository commands through a configured local proxy when direct network access fails.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Proxychains Configuration
use_cases.description: Check local proxy availability, proxychains configuration files, DNS proxying, and common timeout causes.

use_cases.title: Document Controlled Proxy Workflows
use_cases.description: Create repeatable guidance for teams that must route specific tooling through an approved proxy endpoint.

prompt_templates.prompt: A curl or wget command failed with a timeout. Check whether proxychains4 is available and suggest a safe retry plan using my approved local proxy.

prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a user-level proxychains4 configuration for a local HTTP proxy on 127.0.0.1:9910, and explain what each setting changes.

prompt_templates.title: Review Package Manager Proxy Use
prompt_templates.prompt: A package manager cannot reach its registry. Compare direct retry, mirror selection, and proxychains4 usage, then recommend the safest option.

prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a controlled workflow for routing selected developer commands through proxychains4, including approval points, logging, and rollback steps.

faq.question: Does this skill provide a proxy server?
faq.answer: No. It assumes the user already has an approved local proxy service, commonly on 127.0.0.1:9910.

faq.question: Can it proxy every application?
faq.answer: No. Proxychains mainly works with dynamically linked TCP clients and may fail for UDP or static binaries.

faq.question: Is automatic proxy retry always safe?
faq.answer: No. Proxying blocked requests can violate policy, so the user should approve retries first.

faq.question: Why does the skill mention SOCKS proxies?
faq.answer: Proxychains supports HTTP, SOCKS4, and SOCKS5 entries, but the proxy endpoint must be trusted.

faq.question: Does it change system configuration?
faq.answer: The included setup script creates a user-level proxychains configuration. Some documentation examples discuss optional shell wrappers.

faq.question: What should teams review before using it?
faq.answer: Teams should review proxy policy, privileged commands, logging requirements, and approved connectivity test endpoints.
